title: Your Health, Your Life: Getting Started with EIR Space
summary: Your health isn't just about avoiding illness—it's the foundation of everything you do, feel, and experience. When you understand and improve your health, you improve your entire quality of life. This guide shows you how EIR Space puts the power of health understanding in your hands, with tools designed to help you live better, feel better, and take control of your wellbeing.

modules.title: Module 1 • Why Your Health Is Your Greatest Asset
modules.overview: Your health is literally your life. It determines your energy, your mood, your ability to work, play, love, and pursue what matters to you. Yet most of us only think about health when something goes wrong. What if you could understand your health deeply? What if you could see patterns, catch problems early, and make choices that genuinely improve how you feel every day? EIR Space exists to give you that power. Not to replace your doctor, but to help you become an informed, empowered participant in your own health journey.
takeaways: Your health directly impacts every area of your life—energy, relationships, work, happiness.
Understanding your health gives you the power to improve it.
Small, informed changes can dramatically improve your quality of life.
You deserve to understand what's happening in your body and mind.
exercises: Health reflection: Write down three ways your health has affected your quality of life in the past month—both positive and negative.
Health goals: What's one aspect of your health you'd like to understand better? What's one thing you'd like to improve?
Sidebar exploration: Open the sidebar and click through each main section. Don't worry about details—just notice what's available.

Explore different tools to improve your health, like Health Actions, Shadow Work, Health Programs, Habit Tracker and the Feedback Studio. There are 20 different tools to explore, Start with what interests you most, and explore as you go. Focus on curiosity and be open to improvement and understanding yourself. This program will guide you through each area.
homework: Life audit: Think about your typical day. Where does your health help you? Where does it hold you back? Write down your observations.
Health vision: Imagine feeling 20% better than you do now. What would be different? What would you do that you can't do now?
Commitment: Write down one reason why understanding your health matters to YOU. This is your 'why' for using EIR Space.

modules.title: Module 2 • Health Journey: See Your Complete Health Story
modules.overview: Imagine having your entire health history at your fingertips—every doctor visit, every test result, every diagnosis and treatment. No more forgotten details or lost records. No more feeling unprepared at appointments. The Health Journey section brings together your clinical records from Swedish healthcare (1177) and your personal health journal. Together, they create a complete picture of your health over time. When you can see your health story, you can understand it. And when you understand it, you can improve it.
takeaways: Having all your health records in one place eliminates confusion and forgotten information.
Seeing your health history over time reveals patterns you might miss otherwise.
Your personal journal captures what records can't: how you actually feel day-to-day.
Together, records and journal give you the full picture of your health.
exercises: Record loading: If you have Swedish healthcare records, try fetching them from 1177 or loading an EIR file. Explore what's there.
First journal entry: Write a short journal entry about how you're feeling right now. Rate your wellbeing. Notice how simple it is.
Pattern hunting: Look through your records or journal. Can you spot any patterns? Any surprises?
homework: Record exploration: Spend 15 minutes exploring your health records. Filter by category or provider. What do you learn?
Journal week: Commit to journaling daily for one week—even just a sentence or two. At the end, look back. What patterns emerge?
Specific tracking: Choose one area to track (sleep, hydration, or activity) for a week. Notice how tracking affects your awareness.
Doctor prep: Before your next appointment, review your records and recent journal entries. What do you want to discuss?

modules.title: Module 3 • Health Assessments: Know Where You Stand
modules.overview: How do you know if something is a problem worth addressing? How do you track whether you're improving? Health Assessments give you clear, structured ways to understand your current health status. These aren't random quizzes—they're validated instruments used by healthcare professionals. By taking assessments and tracking results over time, you get objective measures of your progress. Assessment results help you focus your efforts where they matter most and give you concrete evidence to share with your care team.
takeaways: Assessments provide objective measures of your health status in specific areas.
Tracking assessment results over time shows whether you're improving.
Assessment results help you prioritize what to work on.
You can share results with your healthcare providers for better care.
exercises: First assessment: Navigate to Health Assessments and take one that interests you. Read your results. What did you learn?
Baseline creation: Take 2-3 assessments in areas that matter to you. Save these as your baselines.
Results reflection: Look at your assessment results. Do they match your intuition? Any surprises?
homework: Comprehensive baseline: Take assessments in each major category (mental health, physical wellbeing, etc.) to establish baselines.
Assessment schedule: Set a reminder to retake assessments in one month. Compare results to your baselines.
Doctor sharing: If you have an upcoming appointment, bring relevant assessment results to discuss with your provider.
Focus selection: Based on your assessments, identify one area to prioritize over the next month.

modules.title: Module 4 • Improve Your Health: Tools & Programs for Real Change
modules.overview: Understanding your health is the first step. The next step is improving it. The 'Improve Your Health' section gives you practical tools and structured programs to create real, lasting change. Whether you want to sleep better, manage stress, build healthier habits, or work through specific challenges, you'll find evidence-based resources here. These aren't generic tips—they're structured approaches based on what actually works, designed to meet you where you are and help you get where you want to go.
takeaways: Real health improvement comes from consistent, focused effort—not random tips.
Health Programs provide structured, step-by-step guidance for specific challenges.
Personal growth tools help with sleep, nutrition, emotions, relationships, and daily wellness.
You can work at your own pace—all progress is saved automatically.
exercises: Program browsing: Explore the Health Programs section. Read descriptions. Which programs interest you?
Tool exploration: Browse the personal growth tools. Try one that catches your attention.
Priority identification: Based on your health goals, which program or tool would help most?
homework: Program commitment: Choose one Health Program to start. Read the first module. Complete the first exercise.
Tool deep-dive: Choose one personal growth tool (sleep, nutrition, emotions, etc.) and explore it thoroughly.
Habit selection: Identify one small health habit you want to build. Use the Habit Tracker to start tracking it.
Weekly review: At the end of each week, review what you learned and practiced. What's working? What needs adjustment?

modules.title: Module 5 • EIR Chat: Your AI Health Assistant
modules.overview: Medical information is confusing. Test results, diagnoses, treatment options—it can feel overwhelming. EIR Chat is your personal AI assistant, available 24/7 to explain, analyze, and help you understand. This isn't generic AI—it's a health-focused assistant that can see your records and journal (in the chat context), giving you personalized explanations and insights based on YOUR health data. Think of it as having a knowledgeable health advisor in your pocket, ready to answer questions, explain medical terms, and help you prepare for healthcare conversations.
takeaways: EIR Chat explains medical terminology in plain language you can understand.
The AI can analyze your health data to identify patterns and trends.
You can prepare for doctor appointments by discussing what to ask.
The AI is a tool to enhance understanding, not replace medical care.
exercises: First AI question: Open EIR Chat and ask one question about your health. It could be about a term, a pattern, or a general question.
Record exploration: Ask the AI to summarize your health records or identify patterns. What does it find?
Appointment prep: If you have an upcoming appointment, ask the AI to help you prepare questions.
homework: Term learning: Identify 5 medical terms from your records that you don't fully understand. Ask the AI to explain each one.
Pattern analysis: Have a conversation with the AI about patterns in your health data. What insights emerge?
Question generation: Use the AI to generate a list of questions for your next doctor appointment. Bring this list with you.
Regular use: Make a habit of asking the AI when you encounter something you don't understand. Build your health knowledge over time.

modules.title: Module 6 • Get Care: From Insights to Action
modules.overview: Understanding your health is powerful. But understanding must lead to action. The Get Care section helps you find care and prepare for appointments. This closes the loop: see your patterns, identify what needs attention, find appropriate care, and arrive prepared to make the most of your appointments. This is where health understanding becomes health improvement.
takeaways: Get Care helps you find appropriate healthcare resources.
Arriving at appointments prepared leads to better care.
exercises: Get Care exploration: Browse the Get Care section. What resources are available?
Appointment preparation: For your next healthcare appointment, prepare using EIR Space: review records, identify questions, note patterns.
homework: Care planning: Think about your healthcare needs. What appointments do you need? What concerns should you address?
Preparation practice: Before your next appointment, do a full preparation: records review, pattern identification, question list, assessment results.
Follow-up habit: After appointments, journal about what you learned and what to track going forward.

modules.title: Module 7 • Your Health Journey: Privacy, Practice, and Progress
modules.overview: You've learned what EIR Space can do for you. Now let's talk about how to make it work long-term: the privacy foundation that makes this possible, the practices that lead to lasting change, and your ongoing health journey. Your health isn't a destination—it's a lifelong journey. EIR Space is designed to grow with you, supporting you through changing needs and challenges. This final module helps you build sustainable health practices and understand the privacy principles that protect you.
takeaways: Your data is truly private—stored on your device, not on servers.
Sustainable health practices are more important than perfect tracking.
Small, consistent efforts compound into significant health improvements.
EIR Space is designed to grow and adapt with your changing needs.
exercises: Privacy review: Read the Privacy page. Understand how your data is protected.
Practice planning: Write down 2-3 health practices you want to build with EIR Space.
First week commitment: Commit to specific actions for your first week of regular use.
homework: Practice launch: Start your planned health practices this week. Even imperfectly—just start.
One-month check-in: Schedule a reminder to review your progress in one month. What's working? What needs adjustment?
Health vision revisited: Look back at the health vision you wrote in Module 1. How does EIR Space help you get there?
Journey commitment: Write a brief commitment to yourself about how you'll use EIR Space to improve your health and quality of life.

aiSupport.systemPrompt: Help the user apply one concrete module step at a time. Do not diagnose. Escalate urgent safety concerns to emergency care.
